text:
maya.ml: Heads-up: hit a sharp throughput cliff when running the q8 bring-up with Triton kernels + cuBLAS mixing on A100 in eu-west-1. baseline (vendor kernels) was fine, but Triton path drops ~45% throughput past 512 tokens.

kumar: Uh — can you paste the exact command and a tiny log snippet?

maya.ml: Sure, run we used:```bash
bench run --model redwood-7b-q8 --kernel triton --mix-cuBLAS yes --batch 8 --max-tokens 1024 --region eu-west-1
```Output (tail):```
[2026-03-19 10:07:12] warmup done
[2026-03-19 10:07:45] steady throughput: 320 tok/s
[2026-03-19 10:09:00] after 512 tokens: 176 tok/s  # cliff
```

rachel_sre: Interesting. Any difference in driver / CUDA version in that region's AMI? eu-west sometimes lags with cuda 12.2 vs 12.3.

maya.ml: AMI shows CUDA 12.3 + cuBLAS 12.3.1. Vendor path used cuBLAS-only kernels, Triton path sometimes dispatches to a mixed cuBLAS+custom kernel (we've seen that before).

jonathan: Could be kernel selection heuristics flipping when seq_len distribution crosses threshold. Also microbatching/grace window could create less packed matmuls => cuBLAS performance collapse. Did you try forcing pure Triton or pure vendor?

maya.ml: Yes: forcing pure vendor keeps stable ~590 tok/s. forcing pure Triton gives 320 tok/s steady (no cliff). The cliff only happens with the "mix-cuBLAS yes" path.

kumar: That suggests the handoff point between custom kernels and cuBLAS is wrong for this payload shape. Two quick checks: 1) set environment VAR KERNEL_DISPATCH_DEBUG=1 to log which kernels are chosen per layer, 2) bump warmup to 250 tokens to stabilize packing.

maya.ml: Did KERNEL_DISPATCH_DEBUG and attached snippet:```
layer 1: triton_custom_fwd
layer 2: triton_custom_fwd
layer 10: cublas_matmul_fwd  <-- handoff
layer 11: cublas_matmul_fwd
```Looks like switching mid-model.

rachel_sre: Mid-model switching is risky for perf. Also check PCIe link speed / GPU topology; eu-west A100s in that pool are PCIe gen4 but sometimes NVLink config differs (affects large GEMM tiling).

ci-bench-bot: uploaded: https://ci.redwood.internal/bench/2490101010-summary (summary table attached). Quick numbers pasted:```
config, tokens, tok/s
vendor-only, 1024, 590
triton-only, 1024, 320
triton+mix, 256, 305
triton+mix, 1024, 176  <-- cliff
```

jonathan: Ok actionable: (A) disable mid-model handoff so either all-triton or all-cuBLAS (prefer consistent path), (B) try FlashAttention v3 for attention ops (it's been more stable when we saw mix failures), (C) add hysteresis to kernel-selector: require >2 consecutive microbatches to flip.

kumar: Agreed. I can push a quick flag to kernel-selector to increase hysteresis and force a single execution backend for the run. Should be low-risk in staging.

maya.ml: I'll re-run with forced flashv3 for attn + selector-hysteresis and report. Also will increase warmup to 300 tokens.

rachel_sre: If that doesn't fix it, let's capture nsight traces (10s window) and GPU metrics (SM util, DRAM bw) at the cliff moment. Also capture cuBLAS workspace size envs.

maya.ml: Re-run started (job 2490102001). Early numbers: steady 585 tok/s for 1024 with flashv3 + hysteresis. Looks promising. Will run overnight across us-east and apac to confirm.

deploy-bot: Note: rolling kernel config change (hysteresis bump) scheduled to canary pool tomorrow 02:30 UTC if tests pass.

jonathan: Nice. Action items: maya - run multi-region overnight and upload traces if any cliff; kumar - make hysteresis flag toggleable per-region; rachel - coordinate NSight trace window if we see regression. :thumbsup:

maya.ml: Will do. Thanks team — will post final numbers tomorrow morning. :pray:
